subject: Scaling cadence and network SLA for isolated GPU farms

Subject: Scaling cadence and network SLA for isolated GPU farms

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, Acme is evaluating a VPC/on-prem private deployment with isolated GPU clusters (customer-managed VPC peering to Redwood control plane). Before we lock an initial commitment, I want us all aligned on the throughput and networking expectations so Procurement and Infra can move in parallel.

High-level ask from Acme (recapped):
- Sustained inference throughput target: ~500 QPS (small-medium payloads, 512 token median).
- Burst/peak headroom: 2k QPS for 3-5 minute windows (10x short bursts).
- 95th percentile tail latency SLO: <200ms end-to-end for generation under sustained load.
- Egress and inter-subnet bandwidth must support KV cache warmups and model weights pulls during scale‑out windows.

What I propose as a first pass (please comment):
1) Committed baseline: capacity to reliably hit 500 QPS with 15% safety margin (i.e., reserved pool sized to ~575 QPS).
2) Burst runway: configured warm pools + autoscale policy to absorb up to 2k QPS for up to 5 minutes with graceful shedding rules (fallback to smaller model variant after 2 minutes).
3) Network commitments: recommend 25 Gbps per cluster control plane link and 40 Gbps for model-serving fabrics for clusters expected to serve bursty workloads.
4) Scaling cadence: staged growth — week 0 baseline, week 2 warm-pool tuning, week 4 sustained-run tests and DR scenario.

Attachments: capacity-request-acme-20261112.xlsx (spreadsheet from Acme with sample QPS shapes).

Can you confirm these numbers align with Acme’s expectations and flag any procurement timing constraints? Once we agree, Marissa will draft the mutual action plan and we’ll share a short prep checklist for your infra team.

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear recap. The numbers look roughly right; our internal perf folks ran a light simulation and 500 sustained QPS seems achievable with the instance families we mapped. A few clarifying points: 
- Burst duration: we need the cluster to absorb up to 5 minutes occasionally, but worst-case we could see cascaded bursts if several frontends retry — is there an order-of-operations you recommend for throttling?
- Model variants: we prefer graceful degradation to a cheaper-but-compatible variant rather than a hard rejection.
- Procurement timeline: we can sign baseline commitments in ~3 weeks if the MAP is in place; procurement@acme.com is on cc for contract timing.

I'll drop our short digest of traffic shapes (attached). Can we schedule a 30-min runbook sync with Infra and EdgeCloud (our network partner) next week?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Scaling cadence and network SLA for isolated GPU farms

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks — digging into the numbers quickly. I ran a rough capacity projection based on the workload profile in the attached CSV. Key notes and recommendations: 

Sizing summary (ballpark):
- Serving nodes: recommend N1: 24xA100-80GB-equivalent GPUs split across 6 pods (4 GPUs each) to hit baseline with headroom; this yields ~600-650 sustained QPS depending on batching config.
- Burst nodes: additional warm pool of 8 GPUs (2 pods) kept in pre-warmed state for fast scale-up (adds ~600 QPS of burst capacity).
- Autoscale policy: scale by pod units with proactive pre-warm trigger at 70% sustained CPU/GPU utilization and predictive lookahead for scheduled peaks.
- Cold-starts: model weight pulls can take 40-90s on noisy networks — recommend a persistent NFS cache on each cluster node group or a replicated local cache tier to reduce weight pulls to <10s.

Networking constraints & suggestions:
- Egress sizing: 40 Gbps per cluster for high-burst customers (dedicated uplink to transit), 10-15 Gbps acceptable for lower tiers.
- Packet loss budget: we must keep loss <0.1% to avoid significant latency tail amplification on KV cache operations.
- MTU & jumbo frames: enable jumbo frames on saturated fabrics to reduce CPU overhead during warmups.

Operational playbook items:
- Warm-pool validation test (runbook script) — schedule load tests week 2 post-deploy.
- Graceful fallback chain: full model -> quantized variant -> condensed prompt template -> throttled token rate (order enforced by serving runtime).
- Observability: expose token-level latency histograms and per-pod KV cache hit rates to the customer dashboard; require 1s sampling granularity for the first 2 weeks.

Attachment: vpc-egress-budget-estimates.csv

I’ll draft a short ops-runbook with commands/thresholds if you want — happy to pair with Infra and EdgeCloud.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

- Add-on burst minutes packaged as a burst pool (prepaid or on-demand) — pricing to be shared in the MAP.
- Onboarding plan: 2-week technical onboarding + 2-week performance ramp + readiness sign-off.

2) Coordinate a kickoff with procurement@acme.com and EdgeCloud next Wednesday 11/24 10:00 PT — provisional invite to follow.
3) Work with Legal to include a network SLO appendix referencing the egress and packet-loss budgets Karthik called out.

Sam — please confirm the kickoff attendee list and any redlines Procurement wants upfront. We’ll hold off on hard commitments until the MAP is accepted, but we can lock the baseline pricing cadence in parallel with your procurement cycle.
